fieldValues.title: Live detector benchmark: a local 7B fits the 60 s step but reads real meetings poorly (2026-11-09)
fieldValues.summary: Run live (every 60 s over the last 180 s of cues), qwen2.5-7b on the 8 GB GPU answers in about 3 to 7 s per window and is precise on a clean scripted meeting (precision 0.86, recall 0.50), but on the real 52-minute meeting only 25% of its flags hold. Its decision flags were right 3 of 3, but it raised only 3 in 52 minutes; actions 0/4, open questions 2/16. haiku, the reference, holds at 55%. For now a local model can propose decisions in the engine, sparingly. Actions, questions and topics need a stronger model or more work. Corrected after an independent review: the numbers below come from the fixed script, with one-to-one gold matching, counted parse failures (none), more judge context, and private results ignored by default.
evidence: Fixture precision is understated: the script holds unplanted real decisions (for example the minutes approved), which count as false positives against the planted gold.

Real meeting (private 52-minute recording, whisper base text, 53 windows, 0 unparsed replies, 0 out-of-window citations), sonnet judge per observation with 3 lines before and 6 after:
- qwen2.5-7b: 24 observations after de-duplication (39 raw), precision 0.25. potential_decision 1.00 (n 3), action_item 0.00 (n 4), open_question 0.13 (n 16), topic 1.00 (n 1). Median 3.0 s / max 5.0 s per window; judge $0.16.
- haiku: 74 observations (154 raw), precision 0.55. Decisions 0.36 (n 11), actions 0.59 (n 17), open questions 0.39 (n 18), topics 0.71 (n 28). Median 6.8 s; $0.05 plus judge $0.45.

The first run (local-lab d5a0726) came from an earlier script version that did not count parse failures and matched gold one-to-many. The re-run found no parse failures, and the overall picture held (qwen 0.19 → 0.25, haiku 0.61 → 0.55).
Gemma 4 E4B (the Tiles default family) could not be tested locally: `ollama pull gemma4:e4b` needs a newer ollama than the decision-logger-ollama container's 0.21.0.
The gemma-3-4b row was not run on the real meeting: the auto-mode classifier refused sending the private transcript to OpenRouter, rightly.
One run per setting. The real-meeting categories have small n (qwen decisions n 3), so per-category figures are indicative only; the overall gap of 0.25 against 0.55 is the robust result.
local-lab detect.mjs at commit 068c7be. A .vtt input is tagged private-* by default, and results/detect.* is git-ignored except fixture rows.
fieldValues.body:
## What it says for the engine (transcribe#6)

The latency question is answered: a 7B on the 8 GB GPU returns well inside a 60 s step (worst window 5 s on the real meeting, 15 s cold). The quality question is not. On real speech qwen over-flags open questions and invents action items. Its decision flags are right but rare (3 in 52 minutes), so its decision recall on real speech is unknown and probably low. That matches the earlier local-lab shape (finding 6fe27de2): the small model reads what is plainly in the words (the scripted meeting) and fails where it needs context (a real conversation).

Recommendation:
- The engine starts with qwen2.5-7b proposing **potential decisions only**, each flag a proposal for a person (decision 24ed7a61), with the model configurable.
- Before settling, upgrade ollama and run Gemma 4 E4B through the same `detect.mjs` (fixture and real meeting), since it is the family a cohort anchor ships.
- A real-meeting gold set (decisions marked by a person) would measure recall, which the judge cannot.
- Actions, open questions and topics wait for a model that holds near haiku's 0.55 on the real meeting, or for prompt work measured here.

Sources: semanticops.com#65, holon semanticops.com#64; owner direction vignettes e9491835 (small models for dreamtime and summaries) and 965499aa.
